topic: does more memory buy low-band cancellation? decimation design study
data: 20 sideways segments (/home/xilinx/pos_side + pos_side16), 14 train / 6 held-out, -12 dBFS digital injection, direct mode
verdict: memory is NOT the limit. Residual in 300-1000 Hz sticks at about -12.8 dB from 63 ms up to 250 ms of memory and gets worse beyond that (over-fitting the measurement noise). The floor is set by coherence (0.87-0.89 at 358-453 Hz), not by taps, so B's 8x decimation option cannot reach the -18..-20 dB needed for a +15..+20 dB usable gain.
ceiling_estimate: with this fixture and architecture the usable gain ceiling is about +11 to +13 dB: the low band saturates near -12.8 dB and the >2.6 kHz band is limited near +11 dB by the full-rate stage
what_would_actually_work: raise coherence or reduce the coupling the microphone sees: a close-talk (headset or lapel) microphone puts the talker about 20 dB above the room at the microphone and drops the speaker-to-microphone coupling at the same time. That is the standard way real PA systems avoid feedback and it needs no RTL change.
